provenance: Each observation is explicitly classified as PURE_XNA_DERIVED metadata or RUBY_MAPPING_QUALIFICATION; never CNA output
derivation: Foundation 40 Graphics.IGraphicsDeviceService. Contract rows are read from the pinned XNA 4.0 Windows metadata of Microsoft.Xna.Framework.Graphics.dll, whose IL declares the interface as public abstract with no base and no other interface, and every one of its nine methods as public hidebysig newslot specialname abstract virtual. Mapping rows apply the documented abstract-module projection policy to that metadata. The producer rows record that completing a contract is not the same as providing one: the pinned metadata names exactly one implementer, GraphicsDeviceManager, which is a deferred partial runtime type here, so nothing in this projection conforms to the service and nothing is registered under it.

observations.note: This is a RUBY_MAPPING_QUALIFICATION row -- a measurement of this projection's own state, which a milestone acting on it is expected to move -- not an XNA fact. It measured that nothing provides IGraphicsDeviceService for eleven milestones, and it measures the producer now, in the same six elements. Foundation 101 corrected the finding it recorded: docs/graphics-device-service-producer-audit.md concluded that registering a producer would need a material Game/graphics lifecycle redesign, and re-reading GraphicsDeviceManager's own constructor IL is what settled it -- the registration is two AddService calls into GameServiceContainer, a projected managed dictionary nothing in CNA reads, and this manager has answered every member of the service contract since Foundation 96 measured its four events to be relays of the device's own. What the audit got right is untouched and is still measured by the third element: a bare Game registers nothing, and CNA's own container still has no registration route. The fourth element is the new one -- a Game with a manager answers that manager -- the fifth records that DrawableGameComponent is built rather than blocked, and the sixth that no interface on the frontier is producerless any more.
